cards.back: To sort living things into groups by their features.
cards.say: classify. To sort living things into groups by their features.

cards.back: An animal with a backbone.
cards.say: vertebrate. An animal with a backbone.

cards.back: An animal with no backbone.
cards.say: invertebrate. An animal with no backbone.

cards.front: Name the five groups of vertebrates.
cards.back: Mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians and fish.
cards.say: Name the five groups of vertebrates. Mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians and fish.

cards.back: A vertebrate with hair or fur that feeds its young with milk.
cards.say: mammal. A vertebrate with hair or fur that feeds its young with milk.

cards.back: A vertebrate with feathers, wings and a beak. Birds lay eggs.
cards.say: bird. A vertebrate with feathers, wings and a beak. Birds lay eggs.

cards.back: A vertebrate with dry, scaly skin, such as a snake or a lizard.
cards.say: reptile. A vertebrate with dry, scaly skin, such as a snake or a lizard.

cards.back: A vertebrate with moist skin that lives on land and in water, such as a frog.
cards.say: amphibian. A vertebrate with moist skin that lives on land and in water, such as a frog.

cards.back: A vertebrate with gills, fins and scales that lives in water.
cards.say: fish. A vertebrate with gills, fins and scales that lives in water.

cards.front: Is a whale a mammal or a fish?
cards.back: A mammal. It breathes air and feeds its young with milk.
cards.say: Is a whale a mammal or a fish? A mammal. It breathes air and feeds its young with milk.

cards.front: Is a bat a bird or a mammal?
cards.back: A mammal. It has fur and feeds its young milk.
cards.say: Is a bat a bird or a mammal? A mammal. It has fur and feeds its young milk.

cards.back: Yes. It has feathers and lays eggs, even though it cannot fly.
cards.say: Is a penguin a bird? Yes. It has feathers and lays eggs, even though it cannot fly.

cards.back: Yes. It has scaly skin and lays eggs.
cards.say: Is a crocodile a reptile? Yes. It has scaly skin and lays eggs.

cards.back: Insects and spiders. Snails, worms and crabs too.
cards.say: Name two invertebrate groups. Insects and spiders. Snails, worms and crabs too.

cards.front: How many legs do insects have?
cards.back: Six.
cards.say: How many legs do insects have? Six.

cards.front: How many legs do spiders have?
cards.back: Eight.
cards.say: How many legs do spiders have? Eight.

cards.back: A set of questions that helps you identify a living thing.
cards.say: key. A set of questions that helps you identify a living thing.

cards.front: What kind of questions does a key use?
cards.back: Yes or no questions about features you can see.
cards.say: What kind of questions does a key use? Yes or no questions about features you can see.

cards.back: A key that splits into two choices at each step.
cards.say: branching key. A key that splits into two choices at each step.

cards.front: A key asks: Does it have feathers? Which group is yes?
cards.back: Birds.
cards.say: A key asks: Does it have feathers? Which group is yes? Birds.

cards.front: A key asks: Does it have fur? Which group is yes?
cards.back: Mammals.
cards.say: A key asks: Does it have fur? Which group is yes? Mammals.

cards.front: Why is "Is it pretty?" a poor key question?
cards.back: People disagree. A key needs clear features that everybody can check.
cards.say: Why is "Is it pretty?" a poor key question? People disagree. A key needs clear features that everybody can check.

cards.front: Which is a good key question, "Does it have wings?" or "Is it cute?"
cards.back: "Does it have wings?" because you can check it.
cards.say: Which is a good key question, "Does it have wings?" or "Is it cute?" "Does it have wings?" because you can check it.

cards.front: True or false: A spider is an insect.
cards.back: False. A spider has eight legs and is not an insect.
cards.say: True or false: A spider is an insect. False. A spider has eight legs and is not an insect.

cards.front: Which vertebrate group breathes with gills all its life?
cards.back: Fish.
cards.say: Which vertebrate group breathes with gills all its life? Fish.
